issues.legal_issue: Workers who personally perform work may be workmen even when paid by output and permitted to engage assistance, if the relationship and the nature of the work establish employer supervision and control.
material_facts: The workers were professional salt producers who personally worked with their families on plots allotted to them.
The employer’s officers supervised stages of production, tested the brine and salt, and instructed when production could proceed.
The workers were paid according to the quantity of salt produced and accepted rather than by time worked.
The workers could engage and pay additional labour themselves, but they also personally performed the work.
The dispute was referred for industrial adjudication, and the tribunal found the workers to be workmen.
issues.conclusion: The workers were workmen within the meaning of the statutory definition, and the industrial dispute reference was competent.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(s) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, a workman must be employed in the industry, with an employer–employee relationship. The prima facie test is whether the employer has the right to supervise and control not only what work is done but also how it is done; the degree of control varies with the nature of the work. The relevant inquiry is due control and supervision in the circumstances, not whether control was exercised in every detail. Piece-work payment does not by itself make a worker an independent contractor, and a person who undertakes to work personally does not lose workman status merely by taking assistance from others. The Court relied on Mersey Docks and Harbour Board v. Coggins & Griffith (Liverpool) Ltd., Simmons v. Heath Laundry Company, Sadler v. Henlock, Blake v. Thirst, Grainger v. Aynsley, Weaver v. Floyd, and Whitely v. Armitage; it applied sections 2(s) and 10 of the Act.

predicates.industrial_dispute_reference: The proceeding concerns a reference of an industrial dispute for adjudication.
predicates.workers_personally_perform_work: The workers themselves perform the work they have undertaken, even if they also receive assistance from others.
predicates.employer_supervises_work_process: The employer has authority, appropriate to the nature of the work, to supervise and control how the work is carried out.
predicates.workers_are_workmen_for_industrial_dispu: The workers qualify as workmen for the industrial dispute.

issues.definition: When an industrial dispute reference concerns workers who personally perform their work and whose work process is supervised by the employer, the workers are workmen for that dispute.

issues.legal_issue: A tribunal’s finding on whether an employment relationship exists is a factual finding that cannot be set aside in constitutional supervisory proceedings unless it is wholly unsupported by evidence.
material_facts: The industrial tribunal had jurisdiction to decide whether the workers were employees or independent contractors.
The tribunal found that the employer supervised and controlled production through testing, inspections, and instructions at different stages.
Evidence from the employer’s superintendent and a worker described that supervision and those instructions.
The High Court declined to quash the tribunal’s finding, and the matter reached the Supreme Court on appeal.
issues.conclusion: The tribunal’s finding was supported by evidence and could not be disturbed; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Whether the relationship is that of employer and employee or independent contractor is a question of fact. A tribunal’s finding on a factual question within its jurisdiction is not open to challenge under Article 226 merely because it may be wrong; it may be set aside only when it is wholly unsupported by evidence. The Court relied on Ebrahim Aboobakar v. Custodian General of Evacuee Property and applied Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution.

predicates.constitutional_supervisory_proceeding: The proceeding seeks supervisory or writ review of a tribunal’s decision.
predicates.competent_tribunal_decided_employment_st: A tribunal with jurisdiction decided whether the relationship was employment or independent contracting.
predicates.evidence_supports_finding: Evidence in the record supports the tribunal’s factual finding.
predicates.tribunal_finding_not_set_aside: The tribunal’s factual finding is not set aside in the supervisory proceeding.

issues.definition: In supervisory review, when a competent tribunal decides employment status and evidence supports its finding, that finding is not set aside.
